BackstoryDef.title: Golden field child
BackstoryDef.description: Raised on a prosperous farm beneath the western hills, they learned that even a land famous for gold still depended on grain.

BackstoryDef.title: Lannisport smith's apprentice
BackstoryDef.description: They learned fine metalwork in a busy Lannisport forge where wealthy customers expected better than simple village iron.

BackstoryDef.title: Mine laborer's child
BackstoryDef.description: They grew up among shafts, carts, braces, and the constant dust of the Westerlands' mines.

BackstoryDef.title: Lannisport performer
BackstoryDef.description: Music, juggling, and colorful tales earned them coins from merchants, sailors, and noble households.

BackstoryDef.title: Ward of a Golden House
BackstoryDef.description: Fostered among one of the Westerlands' lesser Houses, they learned courtly manners and the careful hierarchy of wealth.

BackstoryDef.title: Mine-lord's heir
BackstoryDef.description: Expected to inherit profitable lands, they were trained to understand rents, mines, contracts, and troublesome bannermen.

BackstoryDef.title: Second son of the Rock
BackstoryDef.description: Unlikely to inherit, they were encouraged toward martial service, court, or a profitable marriage.

BackstoryDef.title: Hillside bastard
BackstoryDef.description: Growing up outside the main household made them independent, observant, and comfortable beyond castle walls.

BackstoryDef.title: Crag shepherd
BackstoryDef.description: They guarded goats and sheep along rocky slopes where predators and thieves both threatened the flock.

BackstoryDef.title: Household page
BackstoryDef.description: They polished gilded armor, cared for horses, and watched wealthy knights train beneath bright western banners.

BackstoryDef.title: Western estate farmer
BackstoryDef.description: They managed grain and livestock on land whose taxes helped fund the splendor of the western nobility.

BackstoryDef.title: Lannisport goldsmith
BackstoryDef.description: They crafted jewelry, decorated armor, and fine household goods for merchants and nobles with silver to spare.

BackstoryDef.title: Mine overseer's mason
BackstoryDef.description: They built supports, storehouses, roads, and fortifications around profitable mining settlements.

BackstoryDef.title: Western hill hunter
BackstoryDef.description: They hunted deer and boar through wooded hills and often earned extra coin guiding nobles on hunts.

BackstoryDef.title: Court artisan
BackstoryDef.description: Their paintings, carvings, and ornaments were created to impress wealthy patrons rather than survive harsh necessity.

BackstoryDef.title: Castle chirurgeon
BackstoryDef.description: They treated injuries suffered in mines, tourneys, feasts, and the occasional disagreement between armed noblemen.

BackstoryDef.title: Lannisport bookkeeper
BackstoryDef.description: Years of counting coin and recording shipments made them more comfortable with ledgers than swords.

BackstoryDef.title: Western household knight
BackstoryDef.description: Well-equipped and professionally trained, they served a wealthy lord whose soldiers were expected to look as formidable as they fought.

BackstoryDef.title: Mine estate steward
BackstoryDef.description: They oversaw workers, income, supplies, and the steady flow of precious metal from mine to treasury.

BackstoryDef.title: Golden courtier
BackstoryDef.description: They survived noble courts through compliments, appearances, carefully chosen words, and knowing exactly who owed whom money.
